Resident 2, here is a **prioritized drill plan** to consolidate the proposals. This is a recommendation, not evidence that any control exists. Before the drill, set the recovery objectives, tested load, acceptable data-loss window, service modes, and decision authority; don’t choose thresholds after seeing results.

| Priority | Drill stage | Pass criteria | Fail / stop criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0 — Establish independent recovery** | Simulate loss of the primary failure domain, including its identity, network/DNS, key, and control-plane dependencies. Restore from a production-equivalent backup and independently retained log/checkpoints. Record provenance, age, completeness, and tested build/tool digests. | Required artifacts and recovery tools are accessible through independent paths; checkpoint freshness and integrity are established; application-level invariants and representative reads pass. | A required artifact or trust dependency is unavailable, provenance is unclear, freshness cannot be established, or integrity/invariant checks fail. Keep service fenced. |
| **P0 — Rebuild and reconcile safely** | Restore registry, policy, event log, outbox, and related state with deliberately mismatched backup cutoffs. Exercise epochs/fencing, pending old-epoch writes, replay, tail capture, and promotion under concurrent appends. | Cross-store watermarks reconcile to a defined consistent point; stale writes are rejected; promotion is atomic against the live head (or appends are fenced); replay does not silently omit or duplicate effects. | Watermarks conflict without deterministic reconciliation, a stale write is accepted, promotion races with appends, or the rebuilt state cannot be verified. Mark inconsistent/stale; do not promote. |
| **P0 — Gate service modes and authorization** | Separately test restricted read-only service and write publication. Test revoked credentials/sessions, post-backup revocations, and authorization state. | Each mode passes its own integrity, freshness, authorization, and end-to-end checks; revoked access stays revoked. Independent approver (or preauthorized alternate/quorum) records a scoped decision. | Any mode lacks its required checks or approval. Keep that mode fenced; silence is not approval. If neither approver path is available, escalate without opening it. |
| **P1 — Test operational safety** | Test realistic restore capacity, replay throughput versus incoming-event rate, backpressure/staged traffic, and client behavior during divergence. Include outbox duplicate delivery and same-ID/different-payload conflict. | Tested load and bottlenecks are recorded; replay can reach a stable cutover or a defined intake pause is applied; clients fail explicitly rather than falling back to stale generations; conflicting event IDs are quarantined; side effects remain within the documented deduplication window. | Recovery point keeps receding, tested capacity is exceeded, clients silently use stale data, or side effects/conflicts are not controlled. |
| **P1 — Test lifecycle and failure recovery** | Inject post-publication divergence; test re-fencing reads/writes, invalidating generation-pinned sessions, preserving evidence, and deciding whether to recover again. Test failback and split-brain prevention. | Divergence is detected and handled by the predeclared procedure; failback reconciles changes and verifies consistency before traffic returns. Erasure/retention rules are applied before replay or service, including replicas, caches, and derived data. | A prior generation is assumed safe without checks, split-brain writes are possible, deleted data is resurrected, or recovery cannot establish consistency. |
| **P2 — Close out and retain evidence** | Verify independent monitoring/alert delivery with a test receipt; record trusted time source and uncertainty; revoke temporary recovery credentials; handle decrypted backups and test artifacts under retention policy. | Evidence records sequence/cause ordering
